title: A message ring in shared memory
hints: Write the header struct with `alignas(64)` on each counter so they sit on separate cache lines. The data area starts right after the header. Everything else is lesson 3.03 with "bytes" instead of "slots": `head` and `tail` count bytes, and a record's size is `(4 + length + 7) / 8 * 8`.
The free-space check must include the wrap padding: if the record does not fit before the end, it needs `toEnd + record` bytes, not just `record`.
requirements: Variable-size records with 8-byte alignment and correct wrap markers.
Full and oversized messages are refused without corrupting anything.
Producer and consumer objects over the same memory agree, including one created with `create` false.
A real producer thread and consumer thread exchange thousands of messages intact and in order.
stretch: Put the ring in a real file mapping (lesson 3.01) and run the producer and consumer as two programs. Add a "messages dropped" counter for a producer that must never wait, and an event the producer sets after sending so the consumer can sleep instead of polling (milestone 4).
